plain.li: I went into the storeroom to count the food and finished counting much too quickly. We need a month's worth, at least.
[fall] The fields have a few weeks left in them. Whatever we don't put away now, we'll be wishing for in winter.

warm.li: I never want to cut anyone's portion in half again. Let's put food by while the fields still give it.

blunt.li: Empty shelves make people stupid and mean. We're already mean enough. Fill them.

cheerful.li: Shelves stacked to the ceiling! Sacks in every corner! A pantry you have to squeeze into sideways!

gloomy.li: Every colony that starved thought it had enough. Let's actually have enough.

cold.li: Hunger is the one threat we can predict to the day. Let's predict it out of existence.

plain.li: Took me most of an afternoon to count it all. That's the good kind of tired.

warm.li: Nobody goes to bed hungry this season. That's worth everything it took.

gloomy.li: Enough food for a month. Now we just have to live that long.

plain.li: I've thrown out more spoiled meat this month than we ate. A cold room with thirty meals in it, and that stops.

warm.li: When someone comes in half-dead from the fields, there should be a meal waiting, not a wait. Let's build a cold store.

blunt.li: The flies are eating better than we are. Cold room, now.

cheerful.li: Picture it: you open the door, a cloud of cold air rolls out, and behind it, dinner!

gloomy.li: Food rots, people get sick, people die. Let's break the chain at the first link.

cold.li: Every spoiled meal is labor we paid for twice. I'd like to stop paying.

plain.li: Thirty meals, all cold, all ours. I checked the door twice.

cheerful.li: I went in just to stand in the cold for a minute. Highly recommended.

cold.li: Spoilage is now negligible.

plain.li: Last raid I was stitching someone up on the dining table, between the salt and the bread. We need real beds for this.
[afterraid] Count the bandages we used this week. Now count what's left. That's why I'm asking for a hospital.

warm.li: When one of us gets hurt, they should wake up somewhere clean, with someone watching over them.

blunt.li: I'm tired of doing surgery by bad light on a dirty floor. Give me a hospital or stop bleeding.

cheerful.li: Three beds, clean sheets, a whole shelf of medicine! It'll be the nicest room nobody wants to be in!

gloomy.li: Everyone ends up on a sickbed sooner or later. It might as well be a clean one.

cold.li: Infection kills more of our wounded than the wounds do. A clean room changes that.

plain.li: Beds made, medicine sorted. I'm going to stand here and admire it until someone gets shot.

warm.li: Whoever's next in one of these beds, I hope it's only for a scratch.

cold.li: Medical capacity is adequate. I'll be keeping track of who uses it most.

plain.li: I haven't been alone with my own thoughts since I got here. Rooms. One each.

warm.li: Some of us cry at night and pretend we don't. A room each would let us stop pretending.

blunt.li: I know what every one of you sounds like asleep. I'd like to forget. Build walls.

cheerful.li: Private rooms! I'll finally find out what I'm like when nobody's watching!

gloomy.li: There's no privacy in a barracks, not even for grief. I'd like somewhere to fall apart quietly.

cold.li: Shared rooms mean shared diseases and shared grudges. Separate the beds.

plain.li: I closed my door last night just to hear it click. Then I did it again.

blunt.li: Now knock before you come in. All of you.

gloomy.li: My own room. Now I can be miserable in private, like a civilized person.

plain.li: We eat together three times a day. Let's do it somewhere that makes us want to stay at the table.

warm.li: I want a room where we toast the good days and sit together through the bad ones.

blunt.li: Visitors walk in, look at our dining room, and pity us. I can see it on their faces.

cheerful.li: A long table, candles, something on the walls worth staring at! I want to feel like a lord at dinner!

gloomy.li: Most of our last meals will be eaten in that room. Let's make it worth it.

cold.li: The room we use most should be the room we invest in most. It's simple arithmetic.

plain.li: Look at it. You walk in here and you sit up straighter.

blunt.li: Nobody eats with their hands in here. I mean it.

cheerful.li: I've eaten three meals in here today and I'm thinking about a fourth, just for the atmosphere!

plain.li: I've played the same game of horseshoes so many times I've started losing on purpose. We need more to do.

warm.li: Some of us haven't laughed in weeks. A room for games would help more than you'd think.

blunt.li: Bored people break things. Sometimes other people. Rec room.

cheerful.li: A whole room for fun! I'll organize tournaments! There will be brackets!

gloomy.li: Without something to look forward to, the days run together until one of them is your last.

cold.li: Idle minds are a security risk. Give them something harmless to do.

plain.li: Five ways to waste an evening, all under one roof. Civilization.

cheerful.li: I lost every single game tonight and had the best time of my life!

gloomy.li: I won a game today. First thing I've won in a long time.

plain.li: Last time they came, half of us were shooting from behind the firewood pile. Let's build some real cover.
[afterraid] We counted the holes in the walls this morning, then we stopped counting. We need better defenses.

warm.li: I keep thinking about who we'd lose if they hit us harder. I'd rather build than grieve.

blunt.li: Next raid, I want to be behind something solid, looking down a long empty field at them.

cheerful.li: Barricades, walls, a nice clear line of fire! It'll be like a fort! A fort that shoots back!

gloomy.li: The raids only get bigger. One day they'll be big enough. I'd like that day to come later.

cold.li: We have things worth stealing and nothing worth fearing. Raiders do that math too.

warm.li: I walked the line tonight. For the first time, I felt like we could protect each other.

cold.li: Our defensive position is satisfactory. I almost look forward to testing it.

plain.li: Three turrets on the approaches. They'll see raiders before we do, and they never ask for a day off.

warm.li: Turrets can take the first hits, so the rest of us don't have to.

blunt.li: I'm tired of being the one who stands in the open. Let a machine do it.

cheerful.li: Three turrets! I'll name them! I'll polish them! I'll be very sad when they explode!

gloomy.li: We're too few to hold every wall. Machines don't need to be brave.

cold.li: A turret costs less than a colonist and complains less. Build three.

plain.li: Turrets are up. Keep out of their line of fire, everyone. They don't know you.

gloomy.li: They'll blow up eventually. Hopefully next to the right people.

plain.li: Six traps where the raiders like to walk. They'll be limping before they ever see our walls.
[lowtech] Sharpened stakes in the long grass. Old trick. Still works.

warm.li: Every raider a trap stops is one I don't have to shoot. I'd like to shoot fewer people.

blunt.li: I want the walk to our door to be the worst walk of their lives.

cheerful.li: Traps! Hidden, sneaky, pointy traps! Just remember where we put them!

gloomy.li: They'll get through eventually. Let's make sure fewer of them do.

cold.li: A trap works while we sleep and costs almost nothing. I see no downside.

plain.li: Traps are set. Everyone learn the safe path, and I mean everyone.

blunt.li: Good. Now we wait.

gloomy.li: Someone's going to forget and step on one. Just don't let it be me.

plain.li: The lights die every night around the same time. Two batteries would carry us to morning.

warm.li: Nobody should be on the operating table when the power cuts out. Let's store some up.

blunt.li: I'm sick of eating dinner in the dark because the wind dropped. Batteries.

cheerful.li: Little boxes full of lightning! Let's get two and fill them right up!

gloomy.li: One cloudy week and everything stops. The heaters, the freezer, all of it. Then us.

cold.li: Power that stops at sundown is half a power grid. Batteries complete it.

plain.li: Batteries are full and humming. The lights didn't even flicker last night.

gloomy.li: Now when the lights go out, it'll be because something worse happened.

cold.li: Power supply is now continuous.

plain.li: Right now I sew clothes on a bench in the hallway. Give me a real workshop and watch what comes out of it.

warm.li: With a proper workshop, nobody here would have to wear rags into winter again.

blunt.li: I can't make good things in a bad room. Workshop.

cheerful.li: A workshop with the tools hung on the wall, each in its own outline! I've dreamed about the outlines!

gloomy.li: Our gear's held together with string and hope, and we're running low on hope.

cold.li: Our equipment wears out faster than we replace it. That trend ends badly.

plain.li: Two stations, good light, a door that shuts. I could work in here forever.

blunt.li: Nobody touches my tools. Ever.

cheerful.li: I made a thing in the workshop! It's not a very good thing, but it's the first of many!

plain.li: We look at bare walls all day. I want to look at something someone made on purpose, just because it was beautiful.

warm.li: A sculpture where we eat would give us something to talk about besides raids.

blunt.li: Our walls are ugly. Our faces are ugly. Let's at least fix the walls.

cheerful.li: Three pieces of art! One serious, one strange, and one of the cook, unflattering!

gloomy.li: Someday people will dig this place up. I want them to find more than bones.

cold.li: People are calmer in pleasant rooms, and calm people make fewer mistakes. Three pieces of art.

plain.li: Someone just stood in front of one of them for five minutes without saying a word. That's the point.

blunt.li: Nobody hang anything on the sculptures. They're not coat hooks.

cheerful.li: I've been calling it a gallery and nobody has stopped me!

plain.li: There's a whole herd out there walking around for free. Let's bring three in and give them a barn.

warm.li: An animal doesn't care what kind of day you've had. I think we could all use that.

blunt.li: Animals haul, animals fight, animals don't complain. Better than some of you.

cheerful.li: Fluffy ones, big ones, one with a funny face! I want a barn full!

gloomy.li: If the food ever runs out, at least we'll have options.

cold.li: Tamed animals are labor that eats hay instead of meals. Three, minimum.

plain.li: Three new animals and a barn for them. It smells like a real farm in there.

warm.li: They followed me in from the field today. I think they've decided we're family.

cold.li: Three animals tamed. I've already worked out which one is food.

plain.li: There's so much we don't know how to make yet. Give me a lab and some quiet, and I'll start fixing that.

warm.li: Every project we finish is something nobody here has to struggle with again.

blunt.li: We're still doing everything the hard way because nobody's bothered to learn the easy way. Let me.

cheerful.li: A lab! Notes pinned to every wall! The smell of old paper and new ideas!

gloomy.li: The raiders are getting smarter. We'd better get smarter faster.

cold.li: Knowledge is the only resource that doesn't get used up. Invest in it.

plain.li: Three projects done. My head hurts in the good way.

cheerful.li: I learned three whole things! I'm going to explain all of them to everyone at dinner!

gloomy.li: The more I learn, the more I see how close we came to not making it.

plain.li: Every winter we watch the fields die and start counting days. A roof over the crops changes that.

warm.li: Fresh food all year round. The children would grow up thinking winter is just a word.
[winter] Look outside. Nothing's growing. Now imagine walking into a warm room full of green.

blunt.li: The weather's been deciding whether we eat for too long. Let's take its vote away.

cheerful.li: Strawberries in winter! Okay, maybe potatoes in winter! Still!

gloomy.li: One cold snap at the wrong time and the whole harvest is gone. I've seen it happen.

cold.li: Outdoor farming is a gamble with bad odds. Indoors, we set the odds.

plain.li: Whatever the weather does now, the crops don't care.

warm.li: Come and stand in here for a minute. It's the best-smelling room in the colony.

cold.li: Food production no longer depends on the season.

plain.li: Half of us slept in our coats last winter. Let's put heat in the bedrooms this time.
[fall] The nights are getting colder already. Let's get heat into every bedroom before the first frost.

warm.li: I'd like everyone to wake up with feeling in their fingers this winter.

blunt.li: Last winter someone's toes turned black. I'm not naming names. Heat in every room.

cheerful.li: Warm bedrooms! Toasty toes! Waking up without your breath frozen to the blanket!

gloomy.li: I've seen people go to sleep cold and not wake up. I'd rather not see it again.

cold.li: A colonist who loses toes to frostbite is a slower colonist. Heat the bedrooms.

plain.li: I slept with my arms outside the blanket last night. That's how warm it is.

cheerful.li: I took my socks off to sleep. My socks! Off!

gloomy.li: Warm rooms. We'll find something else to suffer about, I'm sure.

plain.li: There's too much work and too few of us. One more person would take a weight off everyone.
[small] There are so few of us that one bad fever would empty the fields. We need more people.

warm.li: There's always someone out there with no one left. We have room. Let's find them.

blunt.li: I don't care if it's a refugee or a prisoner who's changed their mind. We need hands.

cheerful.li: A new face! New stories! Someone who hasn't heard all my jokes yet!

gloomy.li: Every time we lose someone, there are fewer of us to dig the next grave. Let's grow instead.

cold.li: Our workforce is too thin to survive one bad week. Recruit.

plain.li: The new arrival's settling in. Somebody show them where we keep the good meals.

cheerful.li: They laughed at my joke! New people are the best people!

cold.li: One more pair of hands. I'll find out what they're good for.

plain.li: I've seen more scowls this week than smiles. Let's spend a while fixing whatever's making everyone miserable.

warm.li: I want to hear people laughing at dinner again. Let's look after each other for a while.

blunt.li: I'm sick of everybody's moods. Including mine. Let's sort it out before someone throws a punch.

cheerful.li: Let's make this the happiest colony on the Rim! Or at least in the top ten!

gloomy.li: I'd like to remember what this place felt like when we first got here, before it got heavy.

cold.li: Every breakdown costs days of work and sometimes a wall. Raise morale before it costs more.

plain.li: Somebody hummed at dinner tonight. I haven't heard that in a long time.

cheerful.li: Everyone's happy! I checked! Individually!

gloomy.li: Good moods all round. It won't last, but I'm enjoying it while it does.

plain.li: Every time a trader comes through, we can't afford what we need. Let's put silver aside so that stops.

warm.li: One day that silver might pay a ransom for one of us. I'd like it to be there.

blunt.li: Traders can smell poverty. I want them to smell silver.

cheerful.li: A big pile of shiny coins! I just want to look at it sometimes! And maybe buy things!

gloomy.li: The day we need something desperately is the day the trader doubles the price. Let's be ready for it.

cold.li: Silver converts into anything. Hold enough of it, and every problem has a price.

plain.li: Two thousand silver in the vault. Let the next trader try to lowball us.

cheerful.li: I may have sat on the pile. Just for a moment. Very uncomfortable. Worth it.

cold.li: Our reserves are sufficient. From now on we negotiate from strength.

plain.li: Simple meals keep us alive. I want to cook something that makes people close their eyes when they eat it.

warm.li: Cooking well for someone is a way of saying you're glad they're here. Let me say it properly.

blunt.li: I can do a lot better than this slop if someone gives me a kitchen worth the name.

cheerful.li: Real sauces! Seasoning! A meal with more than one color in it!

gloomy.li: Some nights a good meal is the only thing that goes right all day. I'd like more of those nights.

cold.li: A well-fed colonist works harder and complains less. Fine meals are an investment.

plain.li: Twenty fine meals and a kitchen I'm proud of. Come and get it.

blunt.li: Eat it slowly. I didn't cook it for you to inhale it.

cheerful.li: Somebody cried at dinner. Good crying! I'm counting it!

plain.li: Half of us were sick last week, and I know exactly why. The kitchen gets scrubbed, and the butchering goes somewhere else.

warm.li: The cooks work so hard. Let's give them a kitchen they don't have to scrub blood out of first.

blunt.li: There's something's insides on the floor next to the soup pot. I rest my case.

cheerful.li: A kitchen so clean it squeaks! Butchering somewhere else! Everyone keeps their lunch down!

gloomy.li: Food poisoning won't make the history books, but sooner or later it'll kill one of us.

cold.li: Dirt in the kitchen becomes illness in the colony. Remove the dirt.

plain.li: Not one upset stomach this week. Clean kitchen, happy guts.

blunt.li: Anybody who drags a carcass in here goes out with it.

cold.li: Food-borne illness is no longer a significant risk.

plain.li: We keep leaving wounded raiders to die in the mud. A cell would let us turn a few of them into neighbors.
[afterraid] There's a raider out there who's still breathing. Right now our options are a bullet or nothing. Let's build a third.

warm.li: Some of the people who attack us are just hungry and desperate. A bed behind a door would give them a way out.

blunt.li: I want somewhere to put the ones who shot at me, so I can watch them heal.

cheerful.li: A cell! With a bed! We'll run the friendliest prison on the Rim!

gloomy.li: Nobody comes to the Rim on purpose. Some of them just need a reason to stop fighting.

cold.li: A wounded raider in a cell is a worker, a hostage or an organ donor. Options are good.

plain.li: The cell's ready. Strange thing to be proud of, but I am.

warm.li: I put a blanket on the prison bed. It's still a bed.

cold.li: Cell complete. I'll choose the first occupant carefully at the next raid.

plain.li: Traders charge a fortune for beer. We could make our own for the price of some hops and a bit of waiting.

warm.li: When we bury someone, I'd like there to be something to pour for them. Something we made.

blunt.li: Everyone's on edge. Beer won't fix it. Beer will help.

cheerful.li: A brewery! A tasting committee! I volunteer for the tasting committee!

gloomy.li: There's not much joy out here. Some of it comes in bottles.

cold.li: Alcohol is cheap morale and a good trade good. Twenty-five bottles is a sensible stockpile.

plain.li: Twenty-five bottles on the shelf. Nobody touches them until there's something to celebrate. Fine. One each.

blunt.li: Drink responsibly. Or don't. Just don't throw up in the barrels.

gloomy.li: Now we have something to drink at the funerals.

plain.li: Every wall we built in a hurry is made of something that burns. Time to build them properly.

warm.li: I'd like to sleep knowing one stray spark can't take our homes.

blunt.li: Wood walls are just firewood we've agreed to live inside.

cheerful.li: Think of the echo! Stone walls have a wonderful echo! Also they don't burn!

gloomy.li: Lightning, a careless cook, a pyromaniac with a grudge. It only takes one.

cold.li: Wood is temporary. We are not planning to be temporary.

plain.li: Stone, nearly all of it. I knocked on a wall today just to hear it not burn.

cheerful.li: I tried to set a wall on fire to test it! Don't tell anyone! It passed!

gloomy.li: Fireproof. Now it'll have to be something else that kills us.

plain.li: After dark I can't tell the storeroom from the bedroom. A light in every room, please.

warm.li: Nobody should have to feel their way to bed. A light in every room would mean a lot.

blunt.li: I nearly sat on someone in the dark last night. They nearly stabbed me. Lights.

cheerful.li: Light everywhere! No more mystery corners! No more mystery smells! Well, fewer!

gloomy.li: Things move in the dark corners. Probably rats. Probably.

cold.li: We lose minutes every evening fumbling around, and minutes add up. Light the rooms.

plain.li: Not a dark corner left. Found three things I'd lost, and one I wish I hadn't.

cheerful.li: I walked through every room tonight and didn't stub a single toe!

gloomy.li: Now I can see how dirty everything is.

plain.li: One of these days it'll be a wound near the heart, and the hands holding the needle will matter more than anything.

warm.li: I've watched someone die because none of us knew what to do. I want to know what to do.

blunt.li: Whoever stitched my arm last time did it like they were angry at it. Let someone actually learn.

cheerful.li: Doctor training! I'll practice on fruit first! Then volunteers! Mostly fruit!

gloomy.li: Medicine runs out. Skill doesn't. Let's invest in what lasts.

cold.li: A skilled surgeon turns a dead colonist into a merely injured one. That's a very good trade.

plain.li: We have someone who really knows what to do with a needle now. I sleep better.

cheerful.li: Our doctor's the real thing now! Please still try not to get shot!

cold.li: Medical competence achieved. Injuries are now a scheduling problem.

plain.li: Everything we wear is patched and everything we fight with is chipped. Let someone get good enough to fix that properly.

warm.li: I want to make armor good enough that I never have to see one of you bleed through it.

blunt.li: The raiders' castoffs are better than what we make. That's embarrassing.

cheerful.li: One day someone will hold up something I made and ask who made it, and I'll get to say me!

gloomy.li: Bad gear fails at the worst moment. That's the only moment it ever fails.

cold.li: One skilled crafter raises the value of every raw material we own.

plain.li: Made a coat today. Good stitching, good fit. Best thing I've ever made.

blunt.li: Ruin anything I made and I'll make you wear it anyway.

cheerful.li: Someone asked who made their armor! I said me! It was everything I dreamed!

plain.li: Meat and vegetables, pressed and dried. Ugly food, but it'll still be good long after everything else has rotted.

warm.li: If someone has to travel, or the cold store fails in summer, I want there to be food that keeps.

blunt.li: Fresh food is a luxury. Pemmican is a plan.

cheerful.li: Pemmican! The snack that outlives us all!

gloomy.li: Sooner or later we'll have to run. I want something in our packs when we do.

cold.li: Pemmican keeps for months without refrigeration. That is the entire argument.

plain.li: A hundred and fifty packs of pemmican. Tastes like regret, keeps like stone.

cheerful.li: I've built a little wall out of pemmican in the storeroom. It's load-bearing now.

gloomy.li: Enough to survive on. Not enough to enjoy. That's survival, I suppose.

plain.li: We keep dragging our dead out past the fields. They deserve better, and so do the ones who have to walk past them.
[grieving] I don't want to visit a ditch to talk to them. Give them graves.

warm.li: I'd like somewhere to go and talk to the ones we've lost. Even if they can't answer.

blunt.li: I'm tired of tripping over shallow graves in the potato field. Real ones. With markers.

cheerful.li: It's sad, but it doesn't have to be grim! Flowers, a path, somewhere peaceful to sit!

gloomy.li: Three graves. I'd say one for each of us who's next, but there'll be more than three.

cold.li: Bodies in the open draw scavengers. Scavengers draw hunters. Dig the graves.

plain.li: Three graves, dug and marked. It feels wrong to be glad about it, but I am.

warm.li: Someone left flowers already. I don't know who. It doesn't matter.

gloomy.li: There's room now. We'll fill it eventually. We always do.

plain.li: Our noble holds court in a corridor. The next imperial visitor is going to notice.

warm.li: Our noble carries a lot for the rest of us. A proper throne room is the least we can give back.

blunt.li: If I hear one more speech about proper decorum, I'm building the throne myself.

cheerful.li: A throne room! With a carpet! Can we have trumpets? We can't have trumpets, can we?

gloomy.li: The Empire doesn't forgive poor hospitality. Let's not find out what that costs.

cold.li: A satisfied noble brings imperial favor. A throne room is the price of entry.

plain.li: The throne room is done. It's very grand. I feel underdressed walking past it.

blunt.li: There. A chair for sitting importantly in. Happy now?

cheerful.li: I sat on the throne! For one second! Nobody saw! Don't tell anyone!

plain.li: The kids learn whatever the nearest grown-up knows, and sometimes that's the cook. Let's give them proper desks.

warm.li: I want the children to learn things that have nothing to do with surviving, too.

blunt.li: The kids know eleven words for raider and none for please. Fix that.

cheerful.li: School desks! Lessons! Little faces pretending to pay attention! I can't wait!

gloomy.li: We won't be here forever. Somebody has to know how to keep this place going.

cold.li: An educated child is an asset that pays out for decades.

plain.li: Three desks in a row. The children complained immediately, which means it's working.

warm.li: One of the kids read me a whole sentence today. A whole sentence.

cold.li: The next generation is now in training.

plain.li: Every caravan that leaves here thinks a little better or a little worse of us. Let's make it better, on purpose.

warm.li: The next time a trader's caravan limps in hungry, let's feed them. That's how friendships start out here.

blunt.li: Somewhere out there is a faction with more guns than sense. I'd like them on our side.

cheerful.li: Allies! People who wave when they see us coming instead of shooting! Imagine!

gloomy.li: Factions forget favors fast and grudges slowly. Better start piling up favors now.

cold.li: Friendly factions are free reinforcements and reliable buyers. Cultivate one.

plain.li: Their last caravan brought us a gift. Nobody's ever done that before.

cold.li: We now have somewhere to send our problems.

plain.li: Just once I'd like to sit on a chair that somebody cared about while making it.

warm.li: Something well made lasts. I'd like to give this place a few things that last.

blunt.li: Everything here looks like it was built during a raid. Mostly because it was.

cheerful.li: Two beautiful things! Then four! Then the whole colony looks like a museum!

gloomy.li: Most days I can't tell if anything we do matters. A well-made thing would.

cold.li: Quality goods sell for several times their materials. Shoddy goods sell as firewood.

blunt.li: Finally, something in this colony that doesn't wobble.

gloomy.li: Two good things. Raiders will want them. Of course they will.

plain.li: I've made a hundred things that were fine. I'd like to make one that's perfect.

warm.li: I want to make something that makes visitors ask who made it, so I can tell them it was all of us.

blunt.li: I'm wasting my hands on chairs and coats. Let me make something worth stealing.

cheerful.li: I've dreamed about it three nights running! I just need material! And time! And luck!

gloomy.li: Inspiration comes once in a while, and it never stays. If it comes, I want to be ready.

cold.li: Skill without a showpiece is invisible. A masterwork shows it to every trader who comes through.

plain.li: People keep finding reasons to walk past it. I keep catching them.

blunt.li: Took long enough. Worth it. Don't tell anyone I said that.

plain.li: Every log we cut now is one we don't have to dig out of the snow later.

warm.li: I'd like whoever's on night watch to have a fire to come back to.

blunt.li: Trees don't cut themselves, and the cold doesn't care how tired you are.

cheerful.li: A woodpile so high we'll need a ladder! Made of wood! From the woodpile!

gloomy.li: The last thing you burn is your bed. I've heard of colonies that got that far.

cold.li: Running out of fuel in midwinter is a predictable failure. Let's not have it.

plain.li: Smells like sap and sawdust out there. Good smell. Safe smell.

gloomy.li: Three hundred logs. Feels like a lot, until the snow comes.
